<translate>
'''Shenron''' is the Earth dragon. Gather the seven '''Earth Dragon Balls''' scattered around the world spawn of the Overworld, place them together and right-click one to summon him. He grants '''one wish''' per summon, chosen from the list below.
</translate>

<translate>
== Summoning Shenron ==
</translate>
{{Main|Dragons and Wishes}}
<translate>
Find the balls with the [[Special:MyLanguage/Dragon Radar|Dragon Radar]] (Earth), crafted from a Radar's Chip (Earth) and a Radar's CPU (Earth). Place all seven within 5 blocks of each other: once the set is complete the balls glow and chime, and right-clicking one summons Shenron. Only the player who summoned him can make the wish.
</translate>

<translate>
While Shenron is out, the Overworld sky turns into a starry night sky (only visually). If nobody makes a wish, he leaves after 10 minutes. Either way, the balls scatter across the world again.
</translate>

<translate>
== Wishes ==
</translate>
<translate>
Pick one of these wishes each time you summon Shenron:
</translate>

{| class="wikitable"
! <translate>Wish</translate> !! <translate>What you get</translate>
|-
| <translate>Senzu Beans</translate> || <translate>16 [[Special:MyLanguage/Senzu Bean|Senzu Beans]].</translate>
|-
| <translate>Power Boost</translate> || <translate>×100 Attributes: half as Attribute Points and half as the Training Points those Attributes would cost you right now. Hover the wish in the wish screen to see the exact amounts.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Power Pole</translate> || <translate>The [[Special:MyLanguage/Power Pole|Power Pole]] (Nyoibo), a special weapon.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Might Tree Fruit</translate> || <translate>16 Fruits of the Tree of Might.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Namekian Radar CPU</translate> || <translate>4 Radar's CPU (Namek), the CPU used to craft the Namek Dragon Radar.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Saiyan Spaceship</translate> || <translate>A [[Special:MyLanguage/Space Pod|Saiyan Space Pod]].</translate>
|-
| <translate>Reset Passive</translate> || <translate>Clears your racial passive progress: Zenkai boosts and Power Release bonus, assimilations, absorptions and Cell Jrs. See [[Special:MyLanguage/Racial Skills|Racial Skills]].</translate>
|-
| <translate>Re-Customize Character</translate> || <translate>Reopens [[Special:MyLanguage/Character Customization|character customization]]. You can change your appearance and class, but not your race. Your stats and skills are kept.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Change Difficulty</translate> || <translate>Lets you choose your story difficulty again the next time you open the Quest Tree, without resetting your saga progress.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Reset Story Progress</translate> || <translate>Wipes your quest progress across every saga and side quest, so you can play the [[Special:MyLanguage/Sagas|sagas]] again. Your difficulty is kept.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Bring us back to life!</translate> || <translate>Truly revives up to 3 dead players of your choice.</translate>
|-
| <translate>Armor Materials</translate> || <translate>32 Kikono Shards and 64 Iron Ingots.</translate>
|-
| <translate>The Strongest Armor</translate> || <translate>The Strongest [[Special:MyLanguage/Armor|armor]] set (chestplate, leggings and boots).</translate>

<translate>
== Notes ==
</translate>
<translate>
* '''Power Boost''' follows your current stat cost, so it is worth as much late in the game as early on. See [[Special:MyLanguage/Stats and Attributes|Stats and Attributes]].
* After a '''Reset Story Progress''', story rewards shrink on every new run (by default 50% on the second run, 25% on the third, and so on).
* The revive wish only works on players who are dead in the [[Special:MyLanguage/Otherworld|Otherworld]] and online. Revived players lose their halo and are fully alive again.
* The [[Special:MyLanguage/GT Saga|GT Saga]] quest ''The Cracked Dragon Balls'' asks you to summon Shenron.
</translate>
